method: Read every supplied field and reasoned through each key, distractor, rationale, objective and difficulty. Targeted primary-source checks are recorded separately; a reference alone was not treated as validation.
limitations: Not external clinician or psychometric validation
Source verification is targeted; general educational and communication principles were reviewed for internal and clinical coherence.

sourceChecks.finding: Diabetes eye assessment is a screening pathway; this check supports preventive review rather than symptom-triggered care. No exact interval is added to the item.

sourceChecks.method: Primary Hypertension Canada search result inspected
sourceChecks.finding: Standardized preparation, repeated measurements and seated rest reduce variation; nonstandard readings may be elevated. The item should bound the presented value and symptoms.

items.assessment: The screening-before-symptoms key is defensible, but reading glasses as equivalent retinal screening is a conspicuous foil; the task is primarily recognition.
issues: The screening-before-symptoms key is defensible, but reading glasses as equivalent retinal screening is a conspicuous foil; the task is primarily recognition.
proposedChanges: Replace reading-glasses option with reliance on a routine visual-acuity/refraction check, a more credible screening misconception. Either add decision context or label foundation. Add a directly relevant retinopathy source.

items.assessment: Practising escalation addresses the identified knowledge gap, but copying a plan and filing it because signed are implausible nursing alternatives and the key is uniquely detailed.
issues: Practising escalation addresses the identified knowledge gap, but copying a plan and filing it because signed are implausible nursing alternatives and the key is uniquely detailed.
proposedChanges: State the client already demonstrates inhaler technique and routine dosing. Compare symptom-scenario practice with another technique review, a written action-plan explanation, or a scheduled follow-up call using comparable wording.

items.assessment: Structured headache observations are useful, but the only comprehensive option is compared with explicit without-details/only cues.
issues: Structured headache observations are useful, but the only comprehensive option is compared with explicit without-details/only cues.
proposedChanges: Use four actual diary entries of similar length. The best entry should show episode timing, symptoms, triggers and response; alternatives should be credible records that omit different decision-relevant patterns without labeling their omission.

items.assessment: Standardizing daily weight conditions fits the case; averaging household scales and selectively recording the lowest weekly reading are weak alternatives.
issues: Standardizing daily weight conditions fits the case; averaging household scales and selectively recording the lowest weekly reading are weak alternatives.
proposedChanges: Compare plausible schedules and techniques, such as daily before breakfast on one scale, nightly after dinner, morning/evening averaging, and weekly same-day measures. Keep the key concise; explain consistency within the prescribed daily reporting plan.

items.assessment: The intended home-plan features are correct, but the stem is generic and both nonkeys announce omissions or assumptions.
issues: The intended home-plan features are correct, but the stem is generic and both nonkeys announce omissions or assumptions.
proposedChanges: Add concrete home constraints such as no portal access and a reachable telephone service. Present actual contact/escalation arrangements rather than labels such as diagnoses without instructions. Vary correct positions and preserve SATA.

items.assessment: Rehearsing the home plan addresses transition confidence, but indefinite rest and claiming fear disappears are caricatures.
issues: Rehearsing the home plan addresses transition confidence, but indefinite rest and claiming fear disappears are caricatures.
proposedChanges: Establish clinical readiness and the specific concern about warning symptoms. Compare rehearsing a home scenario with providing a written plan, extending supervised visits, and referring to a community exercise group. Explain why the rehearsed response addresses the missing skill.

items.assessment: Recipe adaptation supports the client goal, but the other options all reject or isolate the client cultural preferences.
issues: Recipe adaptation supports the client goal, but the other options all reject or isolate the client cultural preferences.
proposedChanges: Give a concrete usual meal with a sodium source. Compare lower-sodium recipe substitutions, smaller portions, a generic meal plan, and label-reading education, making the client preference and actual source determine the best immediate approach.

items.assessment: Access support is appropriate, but try-harder and assumed fewer tests are implausible professional actions.
issues: Access support is appropriate, but try-harder and assumed fewer tests are implausible professional actions.
proposedChanges: Compare viable access plans, rebooking, education and clinical review. Include transport availability/cost and required monitoring timing so arranging a usable route is clearly best, with similar-length options.

items.assessment: The supplied boom-and-bust activity pattern makes pacing the useful teaching priority. The alternatives reflect recognizable overactivity, avoidance and symptom-contingent workload beliefs; rationales explain their functional limits.
Complete diabetes-review information is correct, but favourable-only values and explicitly excluding nonprescription products disclose the nonkeys; the task lacks application context.
issues: Complete diabetes-review information is correct, but favourable-only values and explicitly excluding nonprescription products disclose the nonkeys; the task lacks application context.
proposedChanges: Use a client with actual fluctuating readings and access difficulties and proposed records or preparation actions. Remove explicit only/excluding signals, or label a strengthened basic preparation item foundation.

items.assessment: Recurring food shortage is appropriately recognized despite current food, but one-meal exclusion and teaching-alone resolution are conspicuous absolutes; this is recognition rather than application.
issues: Recurring food shortage is appropriately recognized despite current food, but one-meal exclusion and teaching-alone resolution are conspicuous absolutes; this is recognition rather than application.
proposedChanges: Make the item a next screening/support decision with realistic competing assessments, or improve the interpretation alternatives and label foundation. Preserve the point that body size and food present today do not establish reliable access.

items.assessment: Housing resource linkage appropriately complements asthma care; all-season windows and withholding symptom reports are implausible alternatives.
issues: Housing resource linkage appropriately complements asthma care; all-season windows and withholding symptom reports are implausible alternatives.
proposedChanges: Compare practical actions such as housing/environmental-resource referral, cleaning advice, inhaler-technique review and trigger tracking. Supply persistent building dampness and correct medication use to explain why structural support is best.

items.assessment: Resident consultation is a sound first step, but preferred language and attractive-kitchen options make it the sole professionally reasonable answer.
issues: Resident consultation is a sound first step, but preferred language and attractive-kitchen options make it the sole professionally reasonable answer.
proposedChanges: Compare plausible planning steps such as surveying residents, booking an accessible venue, adapting existing materials and recruiting facilitators. State that priorities and access barriers have not yet been established.

items.assessment: Client-informed barrier exploration is appropriate, but cultural-refusal attribution and denominator removal are cartoon alternatives.
issues: Client-informed barrier exploration is appropriate, but cultural-refusal attribution and denominator removal are cartoon alternatives.
proposedChanges: Compare reviewing booking/interpreter access with translated reminders, extra clinic hours and outreach calls. Give data that identify a disparity but do not yet establish its cause.

items.assessment: Transport and language access are relevant, but public diagnosis disclosure and attendance-only learning measures are weak distractors and test different constructs.
issues: Transport and language access are relevant, but public diagnosis disclosure and attendance-only learning measures are weak distractors and test different constructs.
proposedChanges: Give a specific community group with transport, hearing/language or schedule constraints. Present concrete class-access arrangements with plausible tradeoffs; keep all options about participation access.

items.assessment: The foundation label is honest. Early identification is distinct from rehabilitation and acute treatment, and the rationale correctly separates screening from diagnosis on a single result.
Rest and standardized repeat measurement are appropriate, but no numeric BP bounds severity and borrowing a relative medication is an implausible nursing recommendation.
issues: Rest and standardized repeat measurement are appropriate, but no numeric BP bounds severity and borrowing a relative medication is an implausible nursing recommendation.
proposedChanges: Specify a moderately elevated reading such as 156/92 mm Hg after rushing, with no concerning symptoms. Compare repeat after appropriate rest, arranging routine follow-up, beginning a home log, or attributing the reading to exertion. Keep diagnosis limits in the rationale.

items.assessment: An accessible referral route is appropriate, but withholding support and marking incomplete access completed are conspicuous wrong actions.
issues: An accessible referral route is appropriate, but withholding support and marking incomplete access completed are conspicuous wrong actions.
proposedChanges: Specify the communication barrier and available accessible service. Compare client-approved text/online referral with telephone coaching, written information and a scheduled callback, using the actual access need to distinguish the key.

items.assessment: Scenario decisions match the objective, but refreshments are irrelevant and the comprehensive key is markedly longer.
issues: Scenario decisions match the objective, but refreshments are irrelevant and the comprehensive key is markedly longer.
proposedChanges: Use plausible outcomes such as symptom-scenario accuracy, confidence ratings, recall of warning signs and completion of a contact plan. Make grammar and length parallel; distinguish recognition/action from self-report and recall.

items.assessment: Community-defined participation and cultural safety are sound, but one-program-fits-all is an advertised error in an otherwise generic good-practice list.
issues: Community-defined participation and cultural safety are sound, but one-program-fits-all is an advertised error in an otherwise generic good-practice list.
proposedChanges: Add a community planning context and replace the assumption option with adopting an existing successful program unchanged, explaining why local selection/adaptation matters. Label foundation if the task remains direct principle recognition.
